The EX-100-KVM-8K KVM Extender is a high-performance connectivity solution designed for multi-media conference halls and professional A/V environments, capable of extending HDMI 2.1 and USB 2.0 signals up to 100 meters (330 feet) over a single Cat6/6a/7 cable using HDBaseT. It supports ultra-high-definition video up to 8K@30Hz (or 8K@60Hz 4:2:0) and 4K@120Hz (4:4:4), with visually lossless VESA Display Stream Compression (DSC) ensuring signal quality. The system includes both a Transmitter (TX) and a Receiver (RX) unit, featuring RS232 pass-through for device control, integrated USB 2.0 extension for KVM functionality, balanced de-embedded audio output via a 5-pin phoenix connector, and convenient one-way Power over Cable (POC) from the RX to the TX unit.
Supports HDMI 2.1 and extends video signals up to 8K@30Hz (or 8K@60Hz 4:2:0) and 4K@120Hz (4:4:4), utilizing visually lossless VESA DSC to maintain high fidelity over the long-distance transmission.

Includes RS232 pass-through for remote device control, along with a balanced de-embedded audio output via a 5-pin phoenix connector on the RX unit for easy integration into professional sound systems.

salesLanguage.headline: EX-100-KVM-8K: gets the signal from one place to another without moving the equipment
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when the source, display, USB device or control point is too far away for a simple local cable.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It lets the room be built around where people and displays need to be, rather than where short cables happen to reach.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Displays away from the rack, lecterns, teaching rooms, meeting rooms and point-to-point signal paths.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Start with distance and what has to travel: video only, video plus USB, audio, control or network.
talkTrack: It solves a distance problem.
If USB is included, it can support cameras, touch displays, keyboards, mice or conferencing peripherals.
It is usually simpler than AV-over-IP when the path is one source to one display.
discoveryPrompts: How far is the source from the display or USB device?

Is this a single fixed route or does it need to switch between many destinations?
avoidPositioningAs: Do not use an extender as a routing system when many sources and many displays need flexible switching.
